title: Bound a residual inside a singular positive moment tensor without an eigenvalue gap
statement: For real finite-dimensional w and Hilbert-valued a,b with integral ||a||^2|w|^2 finite and e=integral||b||^2 finite, let T=integral ||a||^2 w w^T and R=2 Re integral <a,b>w. Then R is in range T and R^T T^+R<=4e, including singular and zero T.

requires: Actual measurable amplitudes a,b, real w in R^n and the two finite integrals
Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the real positive moment matrix
provides: Residual is automatically in the supported range
Quadratic residual control with no uncontrolled smallest-eigenvalue divisor
assumptions: Finite n; no infinite-dimensional closed-range extension
The algebraic bound alone does not imply div T=R
costs: Compute/acquire the actual moments and residual budget e
Transport and boundary identities must be proved separately for applications
contract.units: Consistent amplitude and w units: quadratic form R^T T^+R has the units of e
contract.obstruction: Does not prove the enlarged divergence-free completion, d0, face flux or determinant energy.

evidence.quote: A singular positive moment tensor controls its residual
